key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC on SA516 boiler steel formed the most protective oxide scale and gave the strongest high-temperature oxidation resistance, cutting weight gain by 95.71% versus uncoated steel.
engineering_relevance: For boiler and high-temperature service, the study shows that combining Ni-Cr coatings with TiC reinforcement and HVOF processing can substantially improve durability against cyclic oxidation and spalling.
method: Applied Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings on SA516 steel using HVOF and plasma spray.
Ran 50 cyclic air-oxidation cycles at 900°C to compare oxidation resistance.
Characterized phases and microstructure with XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 95.71% reduction in maximum weight gain for HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC compared with bare SA516, alongside formation of Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO.
watch_item: The results are based on laboratory cyclic oxidation at 900°C, so long-term plant exposure, thermal shock, and coating adhesion under service loading still need validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
